purpose: Teach: 途切れ/有り難い/延長線/掌/讃える/気がつけ/肴/本郷

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、お話が、絶対、途切れた、絶対、こと、絶対、気まずかったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When we were young, there'd be these silences with your father that felt so awkward. Real ones.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Soft attack on the first word. Slow, deliberate pace — the rhythm of someone sorting through old memories. Slight catch in the voice, like emotion unexpected even after all this time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お孫さんからの、本気で、絶対、有り難い、絶対、お手紙、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、宝物よね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. I remember. Letters from the grandchildren — you kept those like treasures, didn't you? Real treasures.
lines.style: Warm, immediate recognition. Her voice settles into the memory comfortably, like slipping into a familiar chair. Gentle insistence — not correcting, affirming. Slight tremor of affection underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家業の、絶対、延長線、絶対、上に、絶対、お父さん、絶対、今を、絶対、考えていたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was younger, I was always thinking about your father's future through the lens of the family business. Do you remember that?
lines.style: Reflective, slightly self-aware. Measured delivery — he's examining his own past thinking without judgment. Quiet admission. The pace slows on 'family business,' as if the weight of it still lingers.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんの、本気で、絶対、掌、絶対、しわが、絶対、増えたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your hands have changed so much — look at all those wrinkles now. Do you see it?
lines.style: Observant, tender. Not mourning or lamenting — noticing with the kind of attention that comes from holding those hands for decades. Voice soft but clear. A slight smile underneath the words.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、職人さんを、絶対、讃える、絶対、お話、絶対、お父さん、絶対、よく、絶対、していたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father used to talk about craftspeople all the time when we were young — do you remember? He really admired them.
lines.style: Warm recollection with a touch of admiration for the memory itself. Gentle emphasis on 'craftspeople.' The pace unhurried — he's savoring the detail. Slight lift at 'admired,' like pride in that memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 気がつけば、本気で、絶対、私たち、絶対、五十年、絶対、夫婦、絶対、続けてきたわよね、あなた
lines.en: And here we are — fifty years married. Can you believe that?
lines.style: Quiet amazement. The words carry weight without being heavy. Slight pause before 'fifty years,' letting the number land. Warm, almost disbelieving tone — wonder that's earned rather than performed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お酒の肴、絶対、ばあさんが、絶対、用意してくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, you'd always have something ready for me with my sake. Those little snacks. Do you remember?
lines.style: Appreciative, almost vulnerable. Voice softens on the details — 'snacks,' 'ready.' Not asking for reassurance, but offering the memory as a gift. Slight trailing-off, inviting her into the warmth of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お父さんと、本気で、絶対、本郷の、絶対、町、絶対、よく、絶対、歩いたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: We walked through Hongo so many times with your father, didn't we? Those streets felt different then.
lines.style: Dreamy, anchored in place and time. Voice opens on 'Hongo' like she's walking those streets again. Gentle, unhurried pace. The final phrase carries a weight — nostalgia for not just a place but a version of themselves.
